prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and bioactive form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement prize for B010 to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. Round 1 showed six matching configurations, but I do not count that as evidence. I re-tested the case on its own terms. The chain is specific and independently confirmed: human incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion and action (Holst), the bioactive truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), receptor and intestinotrophic biology and the therapeutic rationale (Drucker), then long-acting agonists with large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in question. Nothing in the other five statements raised a scientific objection to the discovery, only attribution and wording points, and none of those, as stated, shows that the three names cannot be defended.
statement.case_against: The weakness is still attribution, and the chair is right that it should be treated as a precondition. Priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for the bioactive peptide is not something I can settle from the supplied record, and I will not claim to have verified primary papers or dates. Habener is not a credited name on this ballot, so a swap is not available within the record. Knudsen is excluded only by the three-person cap, and a citation that sounded as if the drugs were an afterthought would misrepresent that. If a documentary check showed Mojsov's step to be derivative of the Habener group's work, I would no longer hold this exact trio, and I would then treat Knudsen as first reserve rather than a different field. A further risk is that a contested allocation will age worse than a cleaner pairing elsewhere on the list.

responses.point: A prize built on a contested allocation may age worse than one for a cleaner pairing such as B020, and the fallback if B010 fails is unclear because B006 has no first-place support and an incomplete attribution.
responses.response: The fallback question is fair and I have changed my alternatives because of it. B020 (Walter and Mori) has the cleanest credit structure on the shortlist and textbook maturity, so I now name it as an alternative in place of B008. I still do not think B010 has reached the point where its attribution should push us there: the unresolved item is one named priority question, not the whole allocation. I also remain unconvinced that B020 is a better prize than B010, since its medical consequence is still mostly conceptual. It is a fallback because it is defensible, not because it is equal in impact.

responses.point: Perlmann will not reduce B006 to June and Sadelain until the Eshhar question is resolved, and asks whether the committee would accept an allocation that excludes the industrial developer, Knudsen.
responses.response: On Knudsen, I accept the exclusion only as a consequence of the cap and the discovery emphasis, and I would reserve her as first replacement if any of the three names weakens. On B006 I agree with you that the missing Eshhar is not a detail. I earlier called the two-name version more defensible, but I would not describe that as a repair, because the ballot cannot supply him. For that reason I keep B006 as an alternative only. If the committee had to fall back on it, I would want that gap stated openly and not hidden in a citation.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that optogenetics is not disqualified as a method, since the Prize has rewarded methods that opened previously intractable questions, and his citation says the work established the incretin axis.
responses.response: I accept that optogenetics has opened circuit questions that were intractable before, but after round 1 I have dropped B008 from my alternatives. The reason is not the method-versus-discovery point, which I still think is arguable. It is that four members treat it as a readiness problem and the credit set is hard to defend: Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck have credible claims against any three-name version. On your citation wording, I prefer saying the discoveries made incretin-based therapies possible over saying they established the incretin axis, because the incretin concept itself is older than the people we are crediting and the claim should not exceed what the three did.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the uniform support risks settling the allocation too quickly, and whether the committee would support a stand-alone B010 or a pairing with a second distinct achievement.
responses.response: I share the worry about settling too fast, which is why I treat the Mojsov-Habener check as a precondition. I still prefer B010 alone. A second part would put three laureates across two achievements and leave one or both parts with one or two people, without improving either allocation, and the fallback candidates have their own attribution gaps (Eshhar for B006, and the unresolved split for B008). A well-defined single achievement is easier to cite accurately than a split prize built mainly to hedge. I would reconsider only if the check weakened Mojsov, and even then I would look at Knudsen before adding a second part.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks B006 second with June and Sadelain only, and asks whether the committee prefers a discovery-only prize or one that also recognises drug development.
responses.response: I prefer discovery with an explicit link to therapy, so the citation says the discoveries made incretin-based therapies possible without naming the drugs. That recognizes the translation without displacing a discoverer. I agree with your two-person reading of B006 on scientific grounds, since Rosenberg's work belongs to adoptive cell therapy in general, but Eshhar is still absent and I would not move B006 above B010 for that reason. I would treat it as the nearest clinical fallback and not as a co-equal second part.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the bioactive peptide is distinct enough from the Habener group's work. I cannot settle this from the supplied record and have not seen primary papers or dates.
Whether Knudsen should enter if any of the three weakens, and whether the cap alone is a sufficient reason for her exclusion in the public statement.
Whether B006, with Eshhar absent, is usable as a fallback, and whether B020 is a better fallback despite less medical consequence.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I report no connection to any credited name on any shortlisted ballot. My documented work is single-cell and spatial genomics, which is not on the shortlist. A recorded co-authorship with Rickard Sandberg, a shared KI affiliation, and a co-authored 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper are not connected to any shortlisted achievement. No recusal is needed.
